st: Divide the beef into 4 equal balls. Press each into a patty about 4 inches wide, with a small dimple in the center.
Season both sides with the salt and pepper just before cooking.
Heat a cast iron skillet or grill over medium-high heat.
Cook the patties for 4 minutes without pressing down. Flip them.
Cook 4 more minutes until they reach 160°F (71°C). Add a cheese slice in the last minute and cover to melt.
Spread the butter on the buns and toast them in the pan for 1 minute.
Build the burgers with lettuce, patty and cheese, tomato, onion and pickles.
Add ketchup and mustard and serve.
Boil the macaroni in well-salted water for 2 minutes less than the package says. Drain.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and butter a 9x13-inch dish.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Slowly pour in the warm milk, whisking nonstop. Cook 5 minutes until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Take the pot off the heat. Stir in [[2.5 cups]] of the cheese, the salt, pepper and mustard powder until smooth.
Fold in the macaroni and pour into the dish.
Top with the rest of the cheese and the breadcrumbs.
Bake for 20 minutes until bubbly and golden. Rest 5 minutes.
Put the chicken in a bowl or bag with the buttermilk and [[2 tsp]] salt. Turn to coat.
Marinate in the fridge for at least [[4 hours]] or overnight.
Mix the flour, paprika, garlic powder, pepper, cayenne and [[1 tsp]] salt in a wide dish.
Lift each piece from the buttermilk, letting extra drip off, and press into the flour mixture until well coated.
Let the coated chicken rest on a rack for [[15 minutes]] so the coating sticks.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 325°F (165°C).
Fry in batches, 4 pieces at a time, for 12 to 15 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and the thickest part reaches 165°F (74°C).
Drain on a rack and rest 5 minutes before serving.
Heat the oven to 275°F (135°C). Remove the thin membrane from the back of the ribs by pulling it with a paper towel.
Mix the sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt and pepper into a rub.
Rub it all over the ribs on both sides.
Wrap the ribs tightly in foil and place on a baking sheet.
Bake for 2 hours 30 minutes until the meat is very tender and the pork reaches at least 190°F (88°C) for pulling-tender texture.
Unwrap and brush the ribs with half the BBQ sauce.
Broil or grill for 5 minutes until the sauce is sticky. Brush with more sauce.
Rest 10 minutes and cut between the bones.
Pat the wings very dry with paper towels.
Toss with the baking powder and salt in a bowl.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Put a rack on a baking sheet and arrange the wings on it.
Bake for 25 minutes, turn, and bake 20 more minutes until crisp and golden. The wings must reach 165°F (74°C).
Whisk the hot sauce and melted butter together in a large bowl.
Add the hot wings and toss to coat.
Serve right away with celery sticks and blue cheese dressing.
Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat for 7 minutes until crisp. Remove and set aside.
Add the butter, onion and celery to the bacon fat. Cook for 6 minutes until soft.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the reserved clam juice, bottled clam juice and potatoes. Add the thyme.
Simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the cream, clams, salt and pepper. Warm gently for 5 minutes without boiling.
Remove the thyme stems, taste, and serve topped with the bacon.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef for 10 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, broth and salt. Bring to a boil.
Lower the heat, cover partly, and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the beans and simmer 15 more minutes until thick.
Taste and adjust salt. Serve hot.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt in a large bowl.
Whisk the milk, egg and [[3 tbsp]] melted butter in a second bowl.
Pour the wet mix into the dry and stir just until combined. Small lumps are fine.
Rest the batter for [[5 minutes]].
Heat a skillet over medium heat and rub with butter.
Pour [[0.25 cup]] batter per pancake. Cook until bubbles form and burst, about 2 minutes.
Flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes until golden.
Stack and serve warm with butter and maple syrup.

ing: tart, such as Granny Smith, peeled and sliced
st: Mix the flour and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Cut in the butter with your fingers until pea-sized crumbs form.
Add the ice water a spoonful at a time until the dough just holds together. Divide in two, flatten, wrap, and chill for [[1 hour]].
Toss the apples with [[0.75 cup]] sugar, the cinnamon, lemon juice, cornstarch and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Roll one dough disc to a 12-inch round and fit into a 9-inch pie dish.
Pile in the apples. Roll out the second disc and lay over the top.
Trim, crimp the edge, cut 5 slits in the top, brush with egg and sprinkle with [[1 tbsp]] sugar.
Bake for 20 minutes, then lower to 375°F (190°C) and bake 40 minutes more until golden and bubbling.
Cool for at least [[2 hours]] so the filling sets.
Bring the water to a simmer in a pot.
Add the hot dogs and heat for 5 minutes, until hot all the way through.
Or grill them over medium heat for 6 minutes, turning, until browned.
Warm the buns in the oven at 300°F (150°C) for 3 minutes.
Place each hot dog in a bun.
Add the mustard and ketchup.
Top with the onion and relish. Serve right away.
Put the ketchup, brown sugar, vinegar and molasses in a saucepan.
Add the Worcestershire, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, pepper and salt.
Whisk everything together until smooth.
Bring to a gentle bubble over medium heat.
Lower the heat and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring often, until thick.
Taste and adjust salt or sugar if you like.
Cool and store in a jar in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.
Whisk the mayonnaise and sour cream in a bowl until smooth.
Slowly whisk in the buttermilk.
Add the garlic, dill, parsley and chives.
Stir in the onion powder, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Cover and chill for [[30 minutes]] so the flavors blend.
Taste and adjust the salt.
Thin with a splash of buttermilk if you want it pourable. Keep in the fridge up to 5 days.
Cut the butter into small pieces and put them in a small saucepan.
Melt the butter over low heat without browning it.
Whisk the hot sauce into the melted butter.
Add the vinegar and garlic powder.
Warm for 3 minutes, whisking, until smooth. Do not boil.
Add the Worcestershire if using and a pinch of salt.
Toss with hot wings or use as a dip. Rewarm gently if it separates.
Stir [[0.5 cup]] active starter with [[1.5 cup]] water in a big bowl. Add [[4 cup]] flour and mix to a shaggy dough. Rest 30 minutes.
Sprinkle [[2 tsp]] salt over the dough and squeeze it in with wet hands. Fold the dough over itself in the bowl 4 times.
Cover and leave at room temperature for 4 to 5 hours, folding every 45 minutes for the first 2 hours, until puffy and 50 percent larger.
Shape into a tight round on a floured counter by pulling edges to the center. Place seam side up in a floured bowl and cover.
Chill in the refrigerator for 12 hours. The cold slow rise builds the famous tang.
Heat the oven to 475°F with a Dutch oven inside for 45 minutes. Flip the dough onto parchment and score the top with a sharp knife.
Bake covered for 20 minutes, then uncovered for 20 minutes until dark mahogany. Cool fully before cutting.
nt: Baked in a covered Dutch oven at 475°F
Best swap: a heavy pot with a lid works if you have no Dutch oven; or bake on a stone with a pan of hot water below.

st: Heat the oven to 425°F. Put a 10 inch cast iron skillet inside with [[2 tbsp]] bacon drippings and heat for 10 minutes until very hot.
Whisk the cornmeal, flour, [[1 tbsp]] baking powder, [[0.5 tsp]] baking soda and [[1 tsp]] salt in a bowl.
Whisk the egg and [[1.5 cup]] buttermilk in another bowl, then pour in the remaining [[1 tbsp]] melted drippings.
Stir the wet mix into the dry just until combined. A few lumps are fine.
Carefully pull out the hot skillet and tilt it to coat the sides. Pour in the batter; it should sizzle loudly.
Bake 20 to 22 minutes until the top is deep golden and a toothpick comes out clean. Cool 5 minutes, then slice into wedges.
nt: Baked at 425°F in a preheated skillet
Best swap: use 1.5 cups milk plus 1 tbsp lemon juice instead of buttermilk, and butter for bacon fat.

st: Heat the oven to 375°F. Toss the sliced peaches with [[0.5 cup]] sugar, [[1 tsp]] cinnamon, [[1 tbsp]] lemon juice and [[1 tbsp]] cornstarch. Let sit 15 minutes.
Pour the peaches and their juices into a 9 by 13 inch baking dish.
Whisk [[1.5 cups]] flour, [[0.25 cup]] sugar, [[2 tsp]] baking powder and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Cut in [[8 tbsp]] cold butter until pea sized crumbs remain.
Stir in [[0.66 cup]] buttermilk just until a shaggy dough forms. Do not overmix.
Drop spoonfuls of dough over the fruit, leaving gaps so the juices can bubble up. Sprinkle with a little extra sugar.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes until the topping is deep golden and the filling bubbles thickly at the edges.
Cool 15 minutes before serving warm with vanilla ice cream.
nt: Baked at 375°F
Best swap: use two 29 oz cans of sliced peaches, drained, with the sugar cut in half, when fresh peaches are out of season.

st: Heat the oven to 350°F. Mix the crumbs, melted butter and sugar and press firmly into a 9 inch pie dish, up the sides.
Bake the crust for 10 minutes until fragrant and set, then cool slightly. Leave the oven on.
Whisk the egg yolks and lime zest for 2 minutes until pale and thick, then whisk in the condensed milk and lime juice until smooth.
Pour the filling into the warm crust and bake for 15 minutes until the edges are set and the center barely jiggles. This bake cooks the yolks safely.
Cool on the counter for 30 minutes, then chill for at least 3 hours until firm.
Top with softly whipped cream and extra lime zest, and slice with a knife dipped in hot water.
nt: Baked at 350°F
Best swap: use bottled key lime juice, or regular lime juice 1 to 1, and crushed digestive biscuits for the graham crumbs.

st: Line a 9 by 9 inch pan with foil and butter it. Have all the other ingredients measured and ready.
Combine the sugar, evaporated milk, butter and salt in a heavy 3 quart pot. Bring to a full boil over medium heat, stirring.
Keep boiling and stirring for exactly 5 minutes, or until a thermometer reads 234°F. Take off the heat at once.
Stir in the chocolate chips until melted, then fold in the marshmallow creme and vanilla until smooth and glossy.
Fold in the walnuts and scrape into the pan. Smooth the top and let it set at room temperature for 3 hours.
Lift the block out with the foil and cut into 1 inch squares.
nt: Boiled to the soft ball stage
Best swap: use [[1 cup]] sweetened condensed milk plus [[1 tbsp]] extra butter for a no-thermometer shortcut, or use dairy-free chocolate and coconut cream.

st: Place the eggs in a pot, cover with cold water, bring to a boil, then turn off the heat, cover and let stand 12 minutes. Chill in ice water and peel.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Cook in a skillet over medium heat for 6 to 7 minutes per side until it reaches 165°F in the center.
Cook the bacon in a skillet over medium heat for 8 minutes until crisp. Drain on paper towels and crumble.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes, then dice. Dice the eggs, avocados and tomatoes.
Whisk [[3 tbsp]] vinegar, [[1 tsp]] Dijon, salt, then slowly whisk in [[0.5 cup]] olive oil until thick.
Spread the lettuce on a platter. Arrange the chicken, bacon, egg, avocado, tomato and blue cheese in neat rows on top.
Drizzle with dressing at the table and toss just before eating.
nt: Pan-cooked chicken and bacon, boiled eggs
Best swap: crumbled feta in place of blue cheese, or skip the bacon and add chickpeas.

st: Cook the rice with [[1.75 cups]] water for 18 minutes and rest for 10 minutes covered.
Warm [[3 tbsp]] rice vinegar, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and [[1 tsp]] salt, then fold into the hot rice. Cool to room temperature.
Mix the surimi with [[2 tbsp]] mayonnaise. Surimi is already cooked and safe to eat as is.
Wrap a bamboo mat in plastic. Lay a half sheet of nori on it, spread a thin layer of rice, and sprinkle on sesame seeds.
Flip the sheet so the rice faces down. Place the crab, avocado and cucumber in a line across the nori.
Roll tightly with the mat, shaping into a firm log. Slice with a wet sharp knife into 8 pieces. Serve with soy and wasabi.
nt: No raw fish: rice steamed, fillings cooked or fresh
Best swap: use cooked shrimp or extra avocado in place of surimi, 8 oz total, to avoid imitation crab.

st: Cut the Spam into 8 even slices, about 1/4 inch thick.
Heat the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Brown the Spam for 2 minutes per side.
Mix [[3 tbsp]] soy sauce, [[2 tbsp]] sugar and [[1 tbsp]] mirin, pour into the pan, and turn the slices until glazed and sticky, about 1 minute.
Sprinkle the rice with furikake and mix. Wet a musubi mold or the empty Spam can and press in about [[0.33 cup]] rice.
Lay a glazed Spam slice on the rice, press down, then lift out the mold.
Wrap a nori strip around the rice and Spam, sealing the end with a drop of water. Serve warm or at room temperature.
nt: Pan-seared and glazed, no raw fish
Best swap: grilled firm tofu or teriyaki chicken in place of Spam, same thickness, for a different protein.

st: Buy sushi-grade ahi labeled safe for raw eating, keep it on ice and below 40°F until the moment you mix it.
Use a very sharp knife to cut the cold tuna into 3/4 inch cubes and place in a chilled bowl.
Whisk [[3 tbsp]] soy sauce, [[1 tbsp]] sesame oil and the pepper flakes in a small bowl.
Add the sweet onion, scallions and sesame seeds to the tuna, then pour on the dressing and fold gently.
Chill for 15 minutes in the refrigerator. Do not marinate longer than 30 minutes or the fish turns mushy and salty.
Spoon over warm rice, top with avocado, and serve right away. Discard any left out more than 2 hours.
nt: No cook: raw tuna, dressed and chilled
Best swap: cubed cooked shrimp or marinated firm tofu in place of ahi, same weight, if you avoid raw fish.

ing: sliced in half to make 4 thin cutlets
st: Pound the chicken cutlets to an even half inch thick between plastic wrap. Season lightly with salt.
Set up three plates: [[0.5 cup]] flour, the beaten eggs, and [[1.5 cups]] panko. Coat each cutlet in flour, then egg, then panko.
Heat [[1 cup]] oil in a wide skillet to 350°F. Test with a panko crumb, which should sizzle at once.
Fry the cutlets 4 minutes per side until deep golden. Chicken must reach 165°F inside.
Drain on a rack, not paper towels, to keep the crust crisp.
For the sauce, simmer [[0.25 cup]] soy sauce, [[0.25 cup]] ketchup, [[2 tbsp]] sugar and the garlic for 3 minutes.
Slice the katsu and serve with two scoops of rice, a scoop of macaroni salad, and the sauce.
nt: Breaded and shallow fried
Best swap: bake at 425°F on an oiled rack for 20 minutes; use pork loin for the chicken for tonkatsu style.

st: Heat the oven to 450°F. Whisk [[2.5 cups]] flour, the baking powder and [[0.5 tsp]] salt, then rub in the cold butter with your fingertips until pea-sized crumbs remain.
Stir in the buttermilk until just combined. Pat the dough on a floured counter into a rectangle 1 inch thick and fold it in thirds twice.
Cut out 6 rounds with a 3 inch cutter, pushing straight down without twisting. Place them touching on a baking sheet.
Bake for 12 minutes until tall and golden. Keep warm under a towel.
Brown the sausage in a large skillet over medium heat, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F, about 8 minutes.
Sprinkle [[0.25 cup]] flour over the sausage and stir for 1 minute. Slowly pour in the milk, stirring constantly.
Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring, until thick enough to coat a spoon. Season with the pepper and the remaining salt. Split the biscuits and ladle the gravy over.
nt: Baked biscuits, skillet gravy
Best swap: use [[1 cup]] milk with 1 tbsp lemon juice in place of buttermilk, and plant based sausage with olive oil for the gravy base.

st: Heat the oven to 325°F. Do not grease the 10 inch tube pan, since the batter needs to grip the sides to climb.
Whisk the flour, [[1 cup]] sugar, baking powder and salt together in a large bowl.
Make a well in the center. Add the oil, yolks, water, vanilla and zest and whisk until smooth.
In a clean bowl, beat the whites with the cream of tartar to soft peaks. Add the remaining [[0.5 cup]] sugar gradually and beat to stiff peaks.
Fold a third of the whites into the yolk batter to loosen it, then gently fold in the rest until no streaks remain.
Pour into the pan and bake for 55 minutes until the top springs back and a skewer comes out clean.
Invert the pan immediately onto a bottle neck and cool 1 hour so it does not collapse.
Run a knife around the edges, release the cake and slice with a serrated knife.
nt: Baked at 325°F
Best swap: 2 cups all-purpose flour minus 4 tbsp plus 4 tbsp cornstarch replaces cake flour.

st: Heat the oven to 350°F and line a 9 by 13 inch pan with parchment, leaving an overhang.
Mix [[1.75 cup]] flour, the powdered sugar and salt, then rub in the butter until a crumbly dough forms.
Press the dough into the pan and bake for 20 minutes until pale golden.
Whisk the eggs, [[1.5 cup]] sugar, lemon juice, zest and [[0.25 cup]] flour until smooth.
Pour over the hot crust and bake for 22 minutes until the filling no longer jiggles in the middle. Eggs are cooked to 160°F this way.
Cool in the pan for 1 hour, then chill 1 hour.
Lift out with the parchment, cut into squares and dust with powdered sugar.
nt: Baked at 350°F
Best swap: use lime juice in place of lemon, 1 to 1, for lime bars.

ing: very cold, from a fresh bottle
st: Chill a tall 12 ounce glass in the freezer for 10 minutes. Everything should be as cold as possible.
Pour [[0.33 cup]] cold milk into the glass.
Add [[2 tbsp]] chocolate syrup, pouring it down the inside of the glass without stirring yet.
Hold the seltzer bottle high and spray it hard into the glass so a thick white foam rises to the top.
Stir briskly with a long spoon, with the tip at the bottom of the glass, until the syrup is mixed but the foam stays tall.
Drink right away through a straw. The foam collapses within a few minutes. There is no egg and no cream in it.
nt: No cook: stir and fizz in a glass
Best swap: oat milk for dairy-free, it foams less, so pour the seltzer from a greater height.

st: Mix [[3 cup]] flour, [[1.5 tsp]] yeast, [[2 tsp]] salt and [[1.25 cup]] warm water until shaggy. Knead 8 minutes until smooth and slightly tacky.
Oil a bowl with [[1 tbsp]] oil, add the dough, cover and let rise 1 hour until doubled.
Coat a 9 by 13 inch dark metal pan with [[2 tbsp]] oil. Press the dough into the pan, stretching to the corners. If it springs back, rest 10 minutes and try again.
Cover and let the dough puff for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 500°F.
Lay the pepperoni over the dough, then pack the cheese cubes all the way to the edges of the pan. The cheese touching the metal is what makes the crisp frico crust.
Simmer [[1.5 cup]] crushed tomatoes with [[1 tsp]] oregano for 5 minutes, then spoon it in stripes over the cheese.
Bake on the lowest rack 14 to 17 minutes until the edges are dark brown and lacy. Run a knife around the edge, lift out and rest 5 minutes before slicing.
nt: Baked at 500°F in a dark steel pan
Best swap: use low-moisture mozzarella mixed with a little white cheddar, 1 to 1, in place of brick cheese.

st: Season the chicken with [[1 tbsp]] Cajun seasoning. Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a Dutch oven over medium high heat.
Brown the chicken 6 minutes, add the sausage, and cook 4 minutes more until browned. Remove with a slotted spoon.
Cook the onion, celery and pepper in the drippings 7 minutes until soft. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, stock and remaining [[1 tbsp]] Cajun seasoning. Return the meat and bring to a boil.
Stir in the rice, cover, and cook on low for 25 minutes without lifting the lid.
Lay the shrimp on top, cover, and cook 8 minutes until pink and firm (145°F) and rice is tender.
Rest 5 minutes, then fluff and serve.
nt: Browned then simmered in one pot
Best swap: use smoked kielbasa for andouille; the oven works too, covered at 350°F for 30 minutes.

ing: ribeye steak, frozen 30 min then thinly sliced
st: Freeze the steak for 30 minutes so it slices very thin. Cut across the grain into paper thin slices.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion with a pinch of salt for 8 minutes until soft and golden.
Push the onions aside, raise the heat to high and add the remaining oil. Cook the steak in a single layer for 2 to 3 minutes until browned and no longer pink.
Chop the steak lightly with two spatulas and mix in the onions. Season with salt and pepper.
Divide into 4 piles and lay 2 slices of provolone over each. Cover the pan for 1 minute until the cheese melts.
Butter and toast the split rolls. Slide a spatula under each pile and scoop it into a roll.
nt: Griddled on a hot skillet
Best swap: use Cheez Whiz for the Philly original, or white American cheese for melt. Use thin sliced sirloin for a cheaper cut.

st: Whisk the mayonnaise, egg, mustard, Worcestershire and Old Bay in a large bowl until smooth.
Gently fold in the crab, crushed crackers and parsley with a rubber spatula. Keep the lumps whole.
Shape into 8 mounded cakes about 3 inches wide. Chill on a plate for 30 minutes so they hold together.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Pan fry the cakes for 4 minutes per side until deep golden.
Make sure they are hot in the center, at least 145°F. Serve with lemon wedges.
nt: Pan fried in butter
Best swap: bake at 400°F for 15 minutes on a greased sheet, and use panko in place of saltines.
